title: Unbounded Resource Consumption via io.ReadAll
platform_conditions: Go 1.x standard library (net/http, io, bufio); applies to all build targets
security_mechanism: io.ReadAll grows its buffer without limit, so a client that streams gigabytes (or lies with a small Content-Length while sending more) exhausts server memory one request at a time. http.Server with zero ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/IdleTimeout accepts connections that never finish, enabling slowloris-style socket exhaustion; missing http.MaxBytesReader removes the platform's per-request cap. The pattern generalizes: make([]byte, n) or make([]T, n) with n from a header allocates attacker-chosen memory instantly, and goroutines or channels spawned per request with no bound leak until the process is killed.

source_sink_clues.source: Request bodies, declared sizes in headers or protocol fields, and the request rate itself.
source_sink_clues.sink: io.ReadAll(req.Body) / io/ioutil.ReadAll with no LimitReader; http.Server{...} without ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/IdleTimeout; make([]byte, n) with n from input; per-request goroutines or channels with no bound

tracking_guards: Require io.LimitReader or http.MaxBytesReader around every request-body read; require http.Server timeout fields be set; require allocation sizes be validated against fixed constants before make; require worker-pool or semaphore bounding for per-request concurrency.
not_candidate_when: The read is wrapped in a LimitReader/MaxBytesReader cap sized to the data's real need, the server sets all relevant http.Server timeouts, the allocation length is clamped to a constant before make, or the endpoint is internal-only behind an enforced network boundary that attacker traffic cannot reach.
public_references: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html
Go standard library: net/http (Server timeouts, MaxBytesReader) — https://pkg.go.dev/net/http
